the molecular mechanisms underlying the transport of the photopigment in the rod photoreceptor cell of the vertebrate retina.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the transport and sorting of rhodopsins in photoreceptor cells.
the molecular basis of retinal degeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C terminus is absolutely essential to ensure the vectorial transport of the protein from the ER to the outer segment.
the carboxyl-terminus is absolutely required for the correct vectorial transport and sorting of rhodopsins in rod photoreceptor cells.

the carboxyl terminal tail of rhodopsine has two functions: (1) it is essential for the transport and sorting of rhodopsins to the outer segment and (2) it is essential to prevent the mis-sorting of rhodopsines to other cellular locations, such as the plasma membrane, and the consequent mislocalization of the rhodopsine to the outer segment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carboxyl terminal domain is essential for the correct vectorial transport and targeting of rhodopsins in rod photoreceptor cells.
the carboxyl terminal domain is essential for the transport of rhodopin in rod photroceptors.
the carboxyl terminal domain is essential for the vectorial transport of the rhodopsin protein in rod photoreceptor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the COOH-terminal tail domain of rhodopsins is absolutely required for correct vectorial targeting to the outer segment of rod photoreceptor cells.
the C-terminal domain of rhodopsins is required for the vectorial transport of the protein in rod photoreceptor cells.
rhodopsin is a highly specialized membrane protein and that it requires its own specific transport machinery to be properly delivered to its correct location in rod photoreceptor cells.
